Graph of the Break-Points of a Term

Source: R/plot_structural.R
plot_breakpoint.Rd

Selects the graph of a break-point term (modelterms7::seg(), modelterms7::jump() or modelterms7::jseg()): the contribution of the term as a function of its variable, with the partial residuals, each break-point as a dashed vertical line, its confidence interval as a bar at the bottom of the graph, and an inset with the profile of the criterion over the position of the break-point.

Usage

plot_breakpoint(
  profile = TRUE,
  test = lr_test(),
  level = 0.95,
  vcov_type = bayesian_vcov(),
  information = distributions7::expected_info(),
  n_grid = 200,
  n_profile = 100
)

Arguments

profile

Whether to draw the inset with the profile.

test

A test object (wald_test(), lr_test() and others), the test inverted for the interval of a break-point.

level

The confidence level of the band, of the intervals and of the cutoff of the profile.

vcov_type

A vcov_method object, the variance of the band.

information

An object from distributions7::expected_info() (the default) or distributions7::observed_info(), the weight of the working response.

n_grid

The number of points of the grid of the variable.

n_profile

The number of positions at which the profile is computed.

Value

A PlotBreakpoint object, inheriting from term_plot.

Details

The contribution and its band are those of plot_effect() for a term whose block moves with its coefficients: \(f(x) = \) modelterms7::term_value() on a grid of the variable, and the band is \(f(x) \pm z_{(1+\text{level})/2}\,\sqrt{J V J'}\), where \(J\) is the block of modelterms7::term_predict() (the derivative of \(f\) in the coefficients) and \(V\) the variance of the coefficients of the term.

The interval of a break-point of a modelterms7::seg() term is confint(fit, parm, test = test, readable = FALSE) on its coefficient, so that test = lr_test() inverts the likelihood ratio test of the position and test = wald_test() gives the Wald interval. The position of a modelterms7::jump() or modelterms7::jseg() term is read off other coefficients and has no coordinate to invert a test on; its interval is the set of positions, connected to the estimate, at which the profile described below stays under the cutoff.

The profile is computed on the working response of the equation, \(y_i^* = f(x_i) + s_i / w_i\), where \(s_i\) is the score of the log-likelihood in the predictor and \(w_i\) the information selected by information. For a position \(\psi_k\) on a grid, with the other positions and the other terms of the equation at their fitted values, \(R(\psi_k)\) is the weighted residual sum of squares of \(y^*\) on an intercept, the linear column and the columns of the term, as computed by modelterms7::seg_profile_rss(). The inset shows \(R(\psi_k) - \min R\), the increase of the criterion in the units of the log-likelihood, against the cutoff \(\chi^2_{1}(\text{level})\) (dotted line). For a gaussian mean it is the likelihood ratio statistic; for other families it is its quadratic approximation at the fit.

A term whose break-points are developed over covariates has one position per observation and no single profile, and a marginal break-point term has a distribution of positions per group; both signal an error.

See also

autoplot.StatmodFit(), plot_effect()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = sort(runif(120, 0, 10)))
dd$y <- 1 + 0.5 * dd$x + 2 * pmax(dd$x - 6, 0) + rnorm(120, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ seg(x, npsi = 1), distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "seg(x, npsi = 1)", data = dd)

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "seg(x, npsi = 1)", data = dd,
                  type = plot_breakpoint(profile = FALSE,
                                         test = wald_test()))
